'''Helen Keil Holt''' (1937 – September 29, 2016) was an American physicist at the [[National Bureau of Standards]], known for her research on [[gas laser]]s and [[quantum metrology]].{{r|obit}}

==Life==
Helen Keil was born in [[West Palm Beach, Florida]] in 1937.{{r|obit}} As a youth she competed in Florida junior championships in tennis, and was nationally ranked as a tennis player.{{r|obit|fellowship}} She became a physics student at [[Barnard College]],{{r|obit}} as well as competing in tennis for Barnard, and graduated in 1958.{{r|fellowship}} She married Lawrence Holt, changing her name to Holt;{{r|obit}} her husband was originally from [[Żarów]] (then in Germany, now part of Poland), had come to the US in 1939 as a young child with his family to escape the Nazis, and was a US Navy aircraft and helicopter pilot who later became a management scientist and systems analyst for the US Post Office.{{r|lawrence}}

Although winning a graduate fellowship to study at the [[University of California, Berkeley]],{{r|fellowship}} she did her doctoral studies in physics at [[Yale University]], staying closer to her husband who was completing an [[M.B.A.]] at [[Columbia University]].{{r|mba}} She completed her Ph.D. at Yale in 1966 under the supervision of [[Vernon W. Hughes]].{{r|obit}} Her dissertation was ''The excitation of the 2<sup>1</sup>S, 2<sup>3</sup>S, and 2<sup>3</sup>P states of helium by electron bombardment''.{{r|diss}}

After completing her doctorate, she became a researcher at the National Bureau of Standards, where she remained for the rest of her career until taking early retirement in 1986. After retiring, she and her husband moved from [[Bethesda, Maryland]] to [[Silver Spring, Maryland]]. She died on September 29, 2016.{{r|obit}}

==Recognition==
Holt was named a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] (APS) in 1977, after a nomination from the APS Division of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics.{{r|aps}}
